notes: OPS.VALIDATE.1 shipped 2026-08-31 as the second phase of the product-recovery sprint. Like OPS.PATCH.1 it is a live production bug fix rather than an audit, plan, preview or shadow experiment: it changes the detector, runner, classifier and downstream consumers that real runs go through, and it is not report-only.

Four reproduced defects. (A) Default Python preflight emitted a bare `pytest`; the active virtualenv owned pytest and PATH did not, so C.A.T.T.U.S could not validate its own repository. (B) A flat solution.py/test_solution.py repository with no tests/ directory and no pytest.ini fell through to `python -m unittest`, which collected none of its pytest functions. (C) `Ran 0 tests` / `NO TESTS RAN` was classified test_failure, reporting a non-event as a defect. (D) detect_repo_language returned typescript while detect_default_preflight_command had no TypeScript branch, so a large TypeScript repository received no_validation_command plus irrelevant C#/Python advice.

Three-way semantics. core/validation_outcome.py defines passed / failed / inconclusive plus the categories that mean 'no code assertion was evaluated': no_validation_command, no_tests_collected, validation_tool_unavailable, and the pre-existing missing_toolchain, validation_environment and unsafe_validation_command. The category decides the outcome, so a runner that exits 0 having collected nothing is inconclusive and a runner that could not start is inconclusive. There is no score, weight or confidence anywhere in it.

Boolean compatibility. Every existing consumer still reads `ok`, and only a genuine pass sets it true. An inconclusive run that executed is ok=False, which keeps automatic patch safety exactly as conservative as it was: an unvalidated patch is still not accepted and still rolls back. The categorical reason survives structurally as `outcome`, `category` and `validation_outcome`, so downstream code and receipts can tell the two apart even though the boolean cannot.

Interpreter strategy. The emitted text is `python -m pytest`, and the legacy shell runner executes a plain python command as argv with sys.executable in front rather than handing it to the shell. That binds validation to the interpreter C.A.T.T.U.S is running under, and avoids quoting an interpreter path through cmd.exe, where a quoted executable beside a quoted argument is mangled. Commands containing shell syntax, or a backslash that POSIX splitting would eat, still go to the shell exactly as before. The safe-argv runner already mapped python to sys.executable. There is no fallback chain: a bare global `pytest` is never attempted afterwards, and nothing is ever installed.

Zero tests. pytest exit code 5 is authoritative; unittest's `Ran 0 tests` and pytest's `no tests ran` / `collected 0 items` are the bounded output markers, consulted only when the exit code does not already say the run failed for another reason - so a collection error at pytest exit 2, which also prints `collected 0 items`, stays the import or syntax error it really is.

Grounding. The review-skip and compiler-grounded gates in core/pipeline.py now ask is_executed_failure_evidence / is_compiler_grounded_category instead of carrying private category lists that included missing_toolchain and validation_environment. A genuine assertion or compiler failure keeps the fast path that worked in the 27-second calc.py field test; an unavailable runner or an empty suite loses it, and an inconclusive preflight also stops contributing the file:line locations CONTROL consumes, because a validation that established nothing has no defect locations to give.

TypeScript. Only a script the repository already declares is ever run, in the deterministic order test, typecheck, check, build - test first because it is the strongest evidence and the script the JavaScript branch already selected, build last because compiling is the weakest of the four. The package manager comes from the repository's own root lockfile (pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, package-lock.json, else npm), and pnpm and yarn were added to the safe-argv allowlist for the same reason npm is on it. Only `<manager> run <script>` is emitted: never install, never npx. A tsconfig.json repository declaring no usable script returns a TypeScript-specific no_validation_command whose hint names package.json scripts, not .csproj files or Python tests. JavaScript detection is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Receipts. The live producers gained an `inconclusive` input: the CHECK.1 receipt result becomes `errored` rather than `failed`, and the worker's declared validation action becomes `not_run` rather than `failed`. Both are existing values in CHECK.1's frozen vocabulary and `errored` is still a failing receipt result, so a required expectation is still not discharged - the receipt merely stops saying the tests failed for a run in which no test existed. CHECK.1, CHECK.2, CHECK.LIVE.1/1B and WORKER.DECL were not promoted, redesigned or made authoritative, and the shadow observer reads the typed outcome the apply path recorded rather than re-classifying any output.

Benchmark blind spot, closed by an executable case rather than another note. The 54 cases hardcode validation_command, so default detection was never exercised. A case may now omit it by setting auto_detect_validation, which routes selection through the shipped detector; omitting it without the opt-in is still a schema error, and a case may not set both. The existing 54 cases were not rewritten and none was added, so the benchmark corpus and its model-call cost are unchanged. Two deterministic integration cases - flat Python pytest and a TypeScript package-script repository, both with no validation_command - select and execute through the production entry points with no provider call.

Deltas: zero model calls, zero network calls, zero installations, zero new patch authority, and no repository traversal added - Python and TypeScript selection reads named root files, one non-recursive glob per pattern and at most one small config read, and the pre-existing rglob count in the C#/Go/Rust branches is pinned by test. CONTROL localization, patch target selection, write authority, CTX.PATCH, CTX.APPLY, human approval and AUTO_PATCH_ENABLED are untouched; a detected validation command grants no authority of its own.

Registry schema limitation, unchanged from OPS.PATCH.1 and deliberately not redesigned here: automation_level has no value expressing 'human-authored production bug fix', so LOCAL_1_PREPARE remains the closest honest value and writes_real_repo=true carries the fact that matters. Human approval is preserved and picker safety was not weakened to accommodate this phase.

Known follow-ups, recorded rather than fixed here. CLI.RUNTIME.1: the interactive CLI's single-line input makes the prose-embedded `Validation command:` directive awkward or impossible to use correctly; a future fix should prefer a typed CLI option or a separate field over more regex parsing in prose. The cli/interactive.py create_session DB/session fallback is likewise a separate runtime/CLI phase. Neither was touched here.

Authority note (§45): validation grants nothing. The only behavioural consequence of the TypeScript branch reaching the existing patch policy is that a TypeScript repository which previously could not be validated at all now satisfies the pre-existing balanced-style precondition has_validation_command. That gate is a restriction, not a grant: control confidence, a known primary language, AUTO_PATCH_ENABLED and require_validation_for_apply are unchanged, and under the new semantics the validation must actually pass - an inconclusive one is ok=False and still rolls back. policy/decision_helper.py was not modified.

Out of scope and untouched: CONTROL.SAFETY.LIVE.1, WAITER.LIVE.1, retrieval/indexing redesign, code_dna indentation, Phantom Limb, WORKER.DECL.2B, and OPS.PATCH.1's byte-preservation semantics, whose rollback fidelity is re-asserted here under an inconclusive outcome.
phases.summary: Live production fix to the real preflight/validation path, and the second recovery phase triggered by the 2026-08-30 black-box field test. Validation used to answer one question where there are three, so a repository whose test runner was missing, a repository with no tests at all and a repository whose tests genuinely failed all arrived downstream as the same 'validation failed', while a runner that executed zero checks and exited 0 arrived as 'validation passed'. The path now reports passed, failed or inconclusive as a categorical fact alongside the legacy boolean: checks ran and passed, checks ran and failed, or validation established neither. Python detection emits 'python -m pytest' bound to the running interpreter instead of a bare PATH pytest, and recognises flat root-level test_*.py / *_test.py repositories, conftest.py and pyproject/setup.cfg pytest configuration alongside pytest.ini and tests/; unittest remains selected when no pytest marker exists. Zero collected tests is its own category from pytest exit code 5 and from unittest's 'Ran 0 tests', and is never a test failure nor a pass. A test runner the interpreter cannot import, and an executable the shell cannot find, are validation_tool_unavailable rather than an import error about the repository. TypeScript gets a real branch that runs a script the repository already declares, through the package manager its own lockfile names, and returns a TypeScript-specific no_validation_command when it declares none. Genuine assertion, compiler and syntax failures keep their grounding semantics; inconclusive outcomes lose them, and stop contributing preflight locations. Explicit user validation still outranks detection, patch safety stays conservative - an unvalidated patch is still not accepted - and OPS.PATCH.1's byte-exact rollback is unchanged. The phase adds no model call, no network call, no dependency installation, no command retry loop, no repository traversal and no new patch authority, and it is not report-only: it modifies the detector, runner, classifier and consumers that production runs go through.

notes: OPS.VALIDATE.2 shipped 2026-09-01 as a live production validation correctness fix in the product-recovery sprint. Like OPS.PATCH.1, OPS.VALIDATE.1, OPS.PATCH.2 and EXEC.AUTH.LIVE.1 it changes code real runs go through; it is not an audit, plan, preview, shadow experiment or report-only layer.

Defect A, reproduced: repository tests ~8,944 (8,966 collected on 2026-09-01), validation command `python -m pytest`, budget 30 s. The command exceeded the budget and production reported `test_failure`. classify_validation_output received only (output, exit_code, command); a stopped pytest run leaves partial output containing `collected N items` and usually a `FAILED ...` line, so the generic test/assertion taxonomy branches matched. The pin `test_partial_pytest_output_looks_like_defect_evidence_on_its_own` asserts that this text, classified without the budget fact, genuinely lands in EXECUTED_FAILURE_CATEGORIES - the set allowed to ground a diagnosis.

Vocabulary: one canonical category, `validation_budget_exhausted`, added to INCONCLUSIVE_CATEGORIES only. `validation_timeout` is deliberately NOT a second synonym. budget_exhausted_info(timeout_seconds) builds the single classifier payload every timeout site returns, so category, reason and hint cannot drift between the legacy shell runner, the safe-argv runner, preflight, the single-file executor and the plan executor. No score, no confidence, and no claim about what the checks would eventually have decided.

Classification order: the budget branch runs FIRST in classify_validation_output, above every branch below it, because each of those is a claim about the repository and partial output would satisfy several of them. Both runners additionally write the fixed marker `validation budget exhausted` into their output and detect_validation_budget_exhausted reads it, so a caller that drops the structural flag still cannot launder a budget into a test failure.

Downstream, by construction rather than by edit: because the category is inconclusive and never executed-failure evidence, core.control_engine's genuine_failure gate, core.pipeline's review-skip and compiler-grounded-fix gates, core.executor's is_inconclusive_category -> validation_environment_failed phase, core.self_correct_loop's stop, core.candidate_sandbox_validation's inherited outcome and core.execution_outcome_telemetry's final_validation_outcome all behave correctly with no category list copied into them. CONTROL receives no failure locations from an inconclusive preflight, which OPS.VALIDATE.1 had already established.

Attempt semantics (§3): a timeout is command_selected=true, command_attempted=true, command_completed=false (exit_code is None), timed_out=true, outcome=inconclusive. It is never represented as `validation not run`. The command did run; it did not finish.

Preflight (§9): a baseline that exhausts its budget is outcome=inconclusive with ok=False and locations=[]. For a DEFECT task the timeout alone establishes no defect. For an EXPLICIT_CHANGE task WAITER.LIVE.1's explicit_change_request basis is unaffected, because feature intent does not depend on baseline failure; nothing erases the explicit change request.

Post-patch (§10): conservative acceptance is unchanged. Only a passing validation keeps a plan on disk, so a post-patch timeout rolls back exactly as before and OPS.PATCH.1 byte fidelity is re-asserted under the new outcome. EXEC.AUTH then reports execution_authorized=true, execution_attempted=true, mutation_observed=true, final_validation_outcome=inconclusive, rollback_performed=true, application_status=rolled_back, patch_applied=false, final_repository_changed=false.

Sandbox (§11): an OPS.PATCH.2 explicit-change candidate whose sandbox validation times out is candidate_validation_status=inconclusive - never failed, never passed - approval_ready=false, real repository unchanged. This required no change to core/candidate_sandbox_validation.py, which already reads the executor's typed validation_outcome.

CHECK.LIVE (§12): live_validation_result already accepted timed_out and already mapped it onto RECEIPT_TIMED_OUT, a value in CHECK.1's frozen vocabulary that is already a failing receipt result; the fact simply had no path to reach it. run_lifecycle now reads the typed validation_timed_out field and the shadow observation carries it. validation_inconclusive stays true alongside it so the worker's declared action remains not_run. CHECK.1 is not redesigned, not promoted, and its vocabulary is not extended.

Budget policy (§5/§6): the global default stays 30 s, pinned by test on both runner signatures. The pre-existing explicit override (run_validation_command_detailed timeout=, SafeValidationCommand.timeout_sec) is preserved and no second timeout configuration system was created. Raising the global budget would have traded false semantics for runaway weak-machine cost.

Defect B, reproduced: CPython validates a cached .pyc against the source's size in bytes and its mtime truncated to whole seconds. A same-size patch inside one timestamp second satisfies both - the exact shape of this project's patches (`return a - b` -> `return a + b`). On CPython 3.14 a same-size, same-mtime replacement of `return "A"` with `return "B"` kept executing the cached "A". Verified rather than assumed (§19): `-B` and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 were both measured against that reproduction and both still observed "A", because they suppress writes and the stale file is already on disk.

Freshness strategy: a fresh empty temp directory per validation execution, supplied as PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX. sys.pycache_prefix redirects the entire cache - reads included - into a mirror tree, and an empty tree has nothing to be stale, so every module is compiled from the bytes currently on disk. The repository's own __pycache__ is not read, not trusted and not deleted; it is simply not consulted. Nothing is traversed to find it: core/validation_bytecode_cache.py never looks at the repository at all, so traversal delta is zero. Applied last in the existing environment construction of both runners, over anything the parent environment or a caller supplied, because an inherited stale prefix is exactly the state being defended against. Command safety, the argv allowlist and the secret scrub are untouched.

Cleanup: shutil.rmtree(ignore_errors=True) inside a context manager's finally, so it runs on the normal, exception and timeout paths alike. Removal is behind an ownership guard requiring both the cattus-validation-pycache- name prefix and containment under the system temp root, so a mangled value can never delete an unexpected path. A cleanup failure leaves a temp directory behind and cannot mutate the repository. subprocess.run kills and reaps the child before re-raising TimeoutExpired, so no validation subprocess outlives the call.

Non-Python validation (§21): unchanged. PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX is inert for go, cargo, node, dotnet and g++, which is why the mechanism needs no per-language branch - the narrowest implementation. No language's command selection was altered; the TypeScript script-order detection is re-asserted by test.

One existing test changed and why: test_the_shadow_adds_no_repository_membership_traversal counted any enumeration outside .agent/ as a repository traversal. On Windows shutil.rmtree walks the directory it removes, so cleaning up our own temp cache registered as a repository walk. The counter now buckets that path separately - the same exception, on the same grounds, that the .agent artifact bundle already had - and the test additionally asserts the extra enumeration is under the temp cache prefix and that enabling the shadow adds none. The claim is unchanged and sharper.

Measured cost: a fresh prefix means the stdlib and project compile once per validation invocation. On this repository's import set, ~0.2 s warm versus ~0.6-0.7 s cold, i.e. ~0.4-0.5 s per validation execution. Recorded rather than hidden; correctness is the invariant.

Deltas: zero model calls, zero network calls, zero repository traversal added, zero repository cache mutation (nothing deleted, nothing written into the source tree), zero execution/write authority change, zero global timeout change, zero test-selection change, zero retrieval or indexing change. Historical artifacts recording test_failure for past timeouts remain readable and were not rewritten.

Deliberately out of scope and untouched, per the phase brief: large-repository retrieval and index cost (T6's ~26 minutes), core.code_dna._classify_indent - kept as the live dogfood retrieval target rather than removed before retrieval is benchmarked - parser/index symbol quality, patch basis, execution authorization, OPS.PATCH.2 semantics, WORKER.DECL.2B, CHECK.2 wiring, affected-tests-only or last-failed test selection, and .pytest_cache metadata, which is a different cache from executed Python bytecode.

Registry schema limitation, unchanged from OPS.PATCH.1 and OPS.VALIDATE.1 and deliberately not redesigned here: automation_level has no value expressing 'human-authored production bug fix', so LOCAL_1_PREPARE remains the closest honest value and writes_real_repo=true carries the fact that matters. Human approval is preserved and picker safety was not weakened.

Pre-existing suite state, recorded for honesty rather than fixed here: 50 tests were already failing before this phase - registry/picker phase-advance assertions that expect an earlier registry head, plus tests/test_context_selection_contract.py::test_production_python_does_not_activate_selector_runtime, which fails on core/direct_context_patch_attachment.py importing core.file_capabilities. None is validation-related and none was touched.

Readiness for retrieval work: retrieval was deliberately not begun. What it inherits is a baseline validation that can say 'the budget ran out' instead of 'the tests failed', which is the precondition for measuring whether a retrieval change helped - previously a slow run and a broken run were indistinguishable in the telemetry.

Scope note, scripts/run_patch_proposal_queue.py: core.worker_runs reaches its _run_validation_command for real worker proposals, validating in a temp clone that carries the source repository's __pycache__ with it, so §17 applies to it. Only freshness was added - its env builder now takes the same fresh PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX, held for the whole multi-segment run and released on every exit path. Its timeout vocabulary was deliberately left alone because it is already truthful: it reports a stopped segment as its own error with validation_ok=false and never produces a classifier category, so there was nothing to launder there.
phases.summary: Live production validation correctness fix for two reproduced truthfulness defects. (A) Timeout laundering: on the C.A.T.T.U.S self-repository black-box task (~8,944 tests, python -m pytest, 30 s budget) the command exceeded its budget and production reported test_failure. classify_validation_output saw only partial output, and partial pytest output carries 'collected N items' plus FAILED lines, so the generic taxonomy branch matched. A budget the validator itself imposed is a fact about the validator, never evidence about the code. One canonical category, validation_budget_exhausted, joins OPS.VALIDATE.1's INCONCLUSIVE_CATEGORIES and nothing else, so every shared predicate - is_executed_failure_evidence, is_compiler_grounded_category, is_inconclusive_category - refuses it with no downstream category list copied or edited: CONTROL grounding, the pipeline review-skip and compiler-grounded gates, the executor's environment-failure phase, the self-correct loop's stop, the OPS.PATCH.2 sandbox verdict and EXEC.AUTH's final_validation_outcome all follow. A timeout is represented as an attempted validation that did not complete (selected=true, attempted=true, completed=false, timed_out=true, outcome=inconclusive), never as validation-not-run, and it can never ground a defect or bind a failure location. Both runners also write a fixed marker into their output as defence in depth. (B) Stale Python bytecode: CPython accepts a cached .pyc when source size and whole-second mtime match its header, so a same-size patch inside one timestamp second could make validation execute pre-patch bytecode - reproduced on CPython 3.14, and -B / PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE were measured and do NOT fix it because they suppress writes, not reads. Each validation execution now gets a fresh empty PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX directory under the system temp root, applied last through the existing environment construction, so the repository's own __pycache__ is not consulted, not trusted and not deleted, and validation bytecode never lands in the source tree. Cleanup is best-effort behind an ownership guard and runs on the timeout path too. The global 30 s budget is unchanged, the pre-existing explicit timeout override is preserved, no second timeout system was created, and conservative patch acceptance, exact rollback, sandbox approval-readiness and execution authorization are untouched. Zero model calls, zero network, zero repository traversal, zero authority widening, no test-selection or retrieval redesign, not report-only.

notes: THREE FACTS. DEFECT.PROBE.LIVE.1 reproduces one claimed symptom; OPS.VALIDATE.3 runs structurally related existing checks; OPS.VALIDATE.1/.2 reports complete repository validation. targeted=passed never rewrites full=inconclusive and user wording says only that the bounded relevant checks passed.

TRIGGER. Only defect_repair_patch plus grounded_defect, full validation inconclusive/validation_budget_exhausted, reproduced independently-oracled pre-patch probe, exact localized target, exact candidate, existing patch safety pass and already-loaded graph. Analysis, explicit-change and passing/genuine-failing full validation do not trigger, preserving T1/T2/T3 and OPS.PATCH.2.

SELECTION. Existing safe preserved user pytest selectors outrank direct test-symbol resolved_call edges, which outrank test-module imports edges. The operation graph is scanned deterministically. No filesystem discovery, rglob/os.walk, index query, graph rebuild, semantic similarity, model call, generated test or model-authored oracle is accepted.

BOUNDS. Production caps are three test files, eight test nodes and 20 seconds total. Too many related checks is inconclusive/selection_budget_exceeded with no globally highest partial pick. Zero checks is inconclusive/no_relevant_existing_checks, never passed.

BASELINE/CANDIDATE. Separate managed sandboxes receive the current candidate-source baseline and exact fingerprint-bound candidate. Both run the immutable check-set fingerprint through current Python -m pytest, safe argv, plugin autoload disabled, cacheprovider disabled and OPS.VALIDATE.2 isolated PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX. Generated files and caches are discarded with each sandbox and the real repository is never the candidate target.

COMPARISON. Baseline pass/candidate pass passes; baseline pass/candidate fail fails. Baseline failed or inconclusive makes the overall result inconclusive with no failure-count score. Missing pytest/tooling is inconclusive. Timeout is attempted but inconclusive/validation_budget_exhausted, never test_failure.

ORACLE INTEGRITY. If the candidate changes a selected test path, evaluation stops as inconclusive/selected_validation_check_modified before sandbox execution. A patch cannot rewrite its oracle and validate itself. Existing test-path patch safety remains a separate earlier defence, including T3.

IDENTITY. Repository identity, candidate fingerprint and immutable check-set fingerprint are recorded. A refinement makes the verdict stale and the pipeline drops the targeted telemetry group without dropping or changing the full-validation or defect-probe receipts.

PROBE SEPARATION. The pre-patch probe result remains a separate telemetry field. Probe success cannot override targeted failure; targeted pass does not say the probe is fixed. Post-patch probe re-execution is not added and remains evidence a future authority policy would have to require separately.

AUTHORITY DELTA ZERO. targeted_validation_authority_effect=none. The runtime records the result but no authorization branch reads it. It cannot set execution_authorized, auto_apply_allowed, write_authority, patch_application_authority or approval_ready, and a targeted pass does not change the full-suite inconclusive fact.
LANGUAGE COVERAGE. Python/pytest only. Other ecosystems are targeted-validation unavailable/inconclusive without changing ordinary whole-repository validation.

FROZEN DELTAS. Zero model calls, network calls, dependency installation, new repository traversal, retrieval/ranking/index semantic change, global-timeout increase, automatic authority widening or core/code_dna.py change. _classify_indent remains unfixed. The capability executes checks and sandboxes candidates, so it is not report-only.

FUTURE POLICY EVIDENCE. A later policy may evaluate reproduced independent pre-patch probe + exact grounding + clean targeted baseline + separately obtained fixed post-patch probe + unchanged existing targeted checks passed + patch safety. OPS.VALIDATE.3 deliberately does not make that policy decision.
phases.summary: Live deterministic targeted repository validation for a defect-repair candidate after complete repository validation was attempted but remained inconclusive because its unchanged global budget expired. A frozen TargetedValidationRequest binds canonical repository identity, the exact OPS.PATCH.2 candidate fingerprint, localized changed paths/symbols, a single immutable set of existing repository-owned pytest checks, graph-backed selection provenance, a 20-second total budget, caps of three test files/eight test nodes, and a disposable-sandbox-only side-effect policy. Selection reads only the already-loaded operation ProgramGraph: preserved safe user pytest selectors first, then test-symbol resolved_call edges to the changed symbol, then test-module imports edges to the changed module. It performs no discovery traversal, graph rebuild, semantic similarity, model selection, generated tests or invented expectations. No relevant checks is inconclusive/no_relevant_existing_checks; an over-cap relation set is inconclusive/selection_budget_exceeded with no partial top-ranked pick. The same check set runs in separate managed baseline and exact-candidate sandboxes through the safe argv runner and OPS.VALIDATE.2 isolated bytecode cache. A failed/inconclusive baseline cannot be laundered into a candidate pass, targeted timeout is inconclusive/validation_budget_exhausted, missing tooling is inconclusive, and a candidate changing any selected test is invalid evidence before execution. Targeted status never rewrites full validation or the separate defect-probe receipt and never grants execution, write, auto-apply or approval authority. Analysis, explicit-change and T1/T2/T3 normal full-validation flows remain unchanged. Python/pytest is the only live framework. No model/network/install/retrieval/global-timeout delta, no repository candidate write, no _classify_indent change, no targeted-auto-apply policy, and not report-only.

notes: PRIMARY DISTINCTION. check_execution_outcome is the immutable OPS.VALIDATE.3 fact; oracle_role is an additive semantic relation to desired behavior. A failed check never becomes passed and a conflicting check is not ignored.

INDEPENDENT BASIS. Desired behavior must already have an accepted explicit-user, repository-contract, existing independent behavioral-contract or deterministic preserved-task-fact basis. Model-only expectation is insufficient_basis, and the same test cannot define both desired behavior and its independent comparison.

BOUNDED EXTRACTION. Only selected named Python test files are read. Direct assert function(args) == literal, != literal and simple boolean assertions with literal/local-literal inputs are supported. Complex assertions are conflict_unresolved. There is no arbitrary semantic interpretation or theorem prover.
NO NAME HEURISTICS. Roles follow target, input and asserted relation. Tokens such as intentionally_broken and defect_remains never participate in classification.

IDENTITY AND STALENESS. Each assessment binds the immutable DEFECT.PROBE.LIVE.2 fingerprint, exact check id/path, entire selected-source SHA-256 and check fingerprint. A changed probe or selected source makes the prior assessment stale. Candidate fingerprint is traceability only, not role semantics.
ORACLE MUTATION. Candidate-modified and candidate-generated selected checks remain candidate_modified_check/insufficient_basis; VALIDATE.ORACLE never rehabilitates the OPS.VALIDATE.3 invalidation.

EVIDENCE MATRIX. Full validation, pre-probe, post-probe, targeted validation and each check's execution/role remain independent bounded facts. post_probe=fixed plus targeted_validation=failed plus defect_preservation_oracle is valid evidence conflict, not inconsistent_input.

GENUINE REGRESSION. A compatible equality check that fails remains failed and is candidate_regression_oracle. A module-related but behavior-unbound failure remains unrelated or unresolved; neither outcome is hidden.

T6. The two selected _classify_indent checks execute the same typed nested two-space input shape and assert 4space while the independently grounded probe expects 2space. Both execution facts remain failed and both roles are defect_preservation_oracle; real tests and core/code_dna.py remain unchanged.

AUTHORITY DELTA ZERO. check_oracle_authority_effect=none. No role grants patch basis, write authority, execution authorization, approval_ready, human approval, auto_apply_allowed or patch acceptance. No policy branch consumes it.

PERFORMANCE AND COMPATIBILITY. Work is linear in at most the already-selected eight checks and reads no other source. Timings expose selected reads, bounded AST parsing and total overhead. T1/T2/T3, OPS.VALIDATE.3, DEFECT.PROBE.LIVE.1/.2, PATCH.BASIS, EXEC.AUTH, ANSWER.GROUND, retrieval, registry/picker, global budgets and broad validation behavior are unchanged. Zero model calls, network calls and repository traversals.

REGISTRY NAMING. VALIDATE.ORACLE.LIVE.1 is a direct live phase in the existing OPS track with sole prerequisite DEFECT.PROBE.LIVE.2. It has no PLAN, READINESS or CLOSE siblings and is not report-only.
phases.summary: Live additive classification of the semantic role of each existing Python/pytest check already selected by OPS.VALIDATE.3 relative to the independently grounded desired behavior in the immutable DEFECT.PROBE.LIVE.2 probe. CheckOracleAssessment keeps the factual check_execution_outcome unchanged and separately records one bounded oracle_role: candidate_regression_oracle, defect_preservation_oracle, compatible_but_nonexclusive, unrelated, conflict_unresolved or insufficient_basis. The classifier reads only selected named test sources, extracts only direct equality, inequality or simple boolean assertions over the same bounded target/literal-input relation, and leaves complex or unbound assertions unresolved without a model. It binds exact check/source and probe fingerprints, marks changed probe/check state stale, and refuses model-only, candidate-modified or generated checks as independent oracles. The evidence matrix preserves full validation, pre/post probe, targeted validation and per-check facts side by side; failed remains failed and fixed remains fixed. T6's two unchanged checks are classified from their actual assertions, not their names, as failed defect_preservation_oracle checks because they preserve 4space while the independent expectation and sandbox observation are 2space. No check ignoring, replacement tests, selection delta, validation-outcome rewrite, _classify_indent fix, retrieval/ranking change, model/network call, patch basis, approval, execution authority or auto-apply policy; not report-only.

notes: TASK-SHAPED COMPOSITION, NOT CLAIM CREATION. SYNTHESIS.1 consumes one preserved INPUT.1 TaskContract, one supplied SynthesisSpecification, explicit ClaimSlotBinding records and frozen CLAIM.1 ClaimAssessment records. It attaches only those existing assessments to predefined slots; it creates no Proposition or ClaimAssessment, performs no lexical, fuzzy, embedding or model matching, and infers no higher-order claim across assessments or slots.

THE PRESERVED USER STRUCTURE IS AUTHORITATIVE. Subject identity and order, explicit rubric labels and order, output format, and explicit constraints are checked against the TaskContract. The output-side preservation gate rejects a dropped, added, renamed or reordered subject; a dropped, added or reordered rubric slot; an output-shape change; changed constraints; an extra slot; and any silent omission of a required or unresolved slot. TaskShape never rewrites the requested answer shape.

EXPLICIT BINDINGS ONLY. ClaimSlotBinding binds slot_id, optional subject_id, proposition_id, expected_assessment_fingerprint and bounded provenance. The assessment fingerprint and proposition identity are re-derived before composition. A slot with declared propositions but no binding reports proposition_binding_required; a bound proposition without its assessment reports missing_claim_assessment. Neither gap is filled by inference.

KNOWN MISSING PROPOSITION-BINDING PRODUCER. No production phase currently creates a SynthesisSpecification or maps preserved rubric slots to proposition ids. SYNTHESIS.1 represents that dependency as incomplete_specification or proposition_binding_required and does not hide a planner inside the composer. Specifications and bindings are hand-supplied by callers and fixtures only.

CLAIM STATUS AND SEMANTIC BASIS SURVIVE. Supported and contradicted assessments populate slots while preserving the exact claim status. Conflicting, insufficient, coverage-incomplete, current-state-unestablished, current-state-inconsistent and inconsistent-input assessments remain visibly unresolved. Multiple differing claim statuses produce mixed_claim_states rather than a composite verdict. analyzer_assessed remains analyzer_assessed; aggregation never upgrades it to deterministic truth.

NO WINNER, SCORE OR CONFIDENCE. Comparison matrices preserve exact ordered subject columns, exact ordered rubric rows and every structural cell, but calculate no majority, tally, weight, rank, score, winner, recommendation or confidence. A request such as 'which is better?' survives only as a DecisionRequirement whose decision_performed property is always false and whose unresolved downstream requirement stays visible.

OUTPUT IS STRUCTURED DATA, NOT RESPONSE PROSE. Supported shapes are single_slot, comparison_matrix, ordered_sections and keyed_report. SynthesisSlotResult holds subject binding, bounded ClaimAssessmentReference records, missing proposition ids, slot status, exact claim statuses, unresolved reasons, semantic basis and binding provenance. render_structured_synthesis_json serializes this structure only; final_response_generated is always false.

DETERMINISM AND TAMPER BINDING. Canonical SHA-256 identities bind the TaskContract, INPUT.1 preservation receipt, SynthesisSpecification, exact claim-slot bindings, every used ClaimAssessment, decision requirement, request and StructuredSynthesis. ClaimAssessment input order is canonicalized while preserved subject and rubric ordinals remain authoritative. Time, randomness and machine state are absent.

AUTHORITY IS NARROW AND REPORT-ONLY. structured_synthesis_authority is true only for a composed result whose structural preservation report passed. Final-response, final-claim, decision, recommendation, evidence-verification, evidence-acquisition, repository-read, network, model-selection, provider-selection, execution, patch and write authority are always false, and human approval is always required.

NO SOURCE, EVIDENCE OR MODEL ACCESS. The module imports only the frozen INPUT.1 TaskContract and CLAIM.1 ClaimAssessment contract plus stdlib hashing, JSON and immutable dataclass helpers. It never imports acquisition payloads, an evidence analyzer, a promotion gate, filesystem, network, subprocess, database, graph, index, selector, model or provider code and never re-verifies semantic relations.

DEEPSEEK FIVE-WAY REGRESSION. The original failure class - a supplied five-way rubric replaced by an agent-selected architecture summary - is closed at this contract layer. Synthetic C.A.T.T.U.S and DeepSeek Harness assessments produce exactly the requested two subjects by five ordered dimensions, including explicit conflict, insufficiency, contradiction and missing-cell states, with no sixth dimension, omitted cell, invented proposition, winner, score, confidence or final prose.

NO LIVE WIRING. No Commander, Instant Run, Project Evolution, Workbench, Mixed Mode, response-generation, planner, patching or other production path imports or calls SYNTHESIS.1. The phase is a pure report-only contract and tests/fixtures are its only consumers. RESPONSE.1 and any separately governed DECIDE phase remain future work and are not implemented or authorized here.

It invents no proposition or claim, performs no cross-claim or cross-slot inference, winner selection, scoring, confidence computation, conflict resolution, evidence acquisition or verification, source read, model call, final-response generation, execution or write, and is not wired into any live product path.

notes: ALLOCATION, NOT CAPACITY. MAX_EVIDENCE_FILES stays 12, MAX_TOTAL_CHARS stays 60,000 and MAX_CHARS_PER_FILE stays 6,000. Every measured improvement happens under the identical caps; tests/test_analysis_evidence_role_balance.py::test_the_global_caps_did_not_move pins all three so a later phase cannot buy the same result with a bigger budget. Post-phase T5 spends 39,158 of 60,000 characters - fewer than the 59,674 the pre-phase order spent on prose.

PRE-PHASE REPLAYED, NOT ASSUMED. The prior selector was re-implemented verbatim and run against the real repository on the canonical T5 prompt rather than inferred: 12 files = 11 project_document + 1 package_manifest, 0 implementation source, 0 TypeScript characters, 59,674 / 60,000 characters. Four of the eleven documents were .zh.md translations of documents already selected. Post-phase, same prompt, same repository, same caps: 6 implementation_source + 4 project_document + 2 package_manifest, 20,241 TypeScript characters, 39,158 / 60,000 characters.

RESERVATION IS INTERLEAVED, WHICH IS THE POINT. Reserving source but reading it last would satisfy the file cap and starve on the character cap: eight 6,000-character files exhaust 48,000 of 60,000. Reserved roles take turns in the reading order, so implementation source is opened before the budget can run out. test_reserved_roles_are_interleaved_so_each_survives_the_character_budget pins this with 20,000-character files on both sides.

THE QUESTION'S OWN WORDS WERE ALREADY PRESERVED AND WERE NOT BEING USED. Role balance alone acquired six real source files that answered nothing: DeepSeekModelsEditor.tsx, DeepSeekOnboardingDialog.tsx, an API gateway and a web bootstrap, because the preserved subjects for the live T5 request are only (deepseek, harness). The words naming what the question is about - agent loop, extension model - sit in the obligations. Feeding obligations into the same bounded token overlap moved the selection to packages/core/agent-loop/src/{index,agent,invariant,constants}.ts. This is still a literal token-overlap count with the same fixed cap of 12 tokens: no frequency, no weighting, no IDF, no model. RETRIEVE ranking is not reopened.

PROFILE DEPENDS ON THE TASK, NOT THE REPOSITORY. The same fixture repository - 40 documents and 30 TypeScript files - selects 0 source files under documentation_explanation and at least 4 under architecture_implementation. The profile is a literal marker match over already-preserved user words; no model classifier was added and the analysis model-call count is unchanged.

NO SECOND SOURCE MAP. Implementation-source detection is core.source_file_policy.SOURCE_ROLE_BY_EXTENSION, which is why .ts classifies as code here for the same reason it does everywhere else, and why README.ts.md classifies as documentation - the real final extension decides. Test/example location reuses core.eligibility_policy.is_test_location plus the two brace-language conventions it does not spell (.test./.spec.); archived material reuses is_historical_location; generated and vendored segments are derived from the module's own existing exclusion prefixes rather than from a new list.

DEMOTION, NOT EXCLUSION, for tests, examples, archived notes, build configuration, generated output and vendored copies. A sample can be the clearest description of an API and generated code is sometimes the only code; what the policy forbids is any of them displacing primary implementation source while primary source exists. Focused tests pin it: 80 spec/example files do not fill the reservation while 6 src files exist, 80 dist/node_modules files do not either, and packages/core/agent-loop/tsdown.config.ts never outranks packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts.

TRAVERSAL DELTA ZERO. Selection consumes the RepositoryInventory production already built and adds no os.walk, rglob or recursive glob. A focused test monkeypatches os.walk to raise and still acquires evidence from a supplied inventory. The pre-existing os.walk fallback for callers that supply no inventory is unchanged.

EXACT REQUEST PRECEDENCE UNCHANGED. Paths the user literally named are taken first, in the order written, before any role is classified, and are never evicted to satisfy a quota. Multi-root remains refused: ../C.A.T.T.U.S and /etc/passwd are still rejected by the unchanged repository-root containment guard, and the live answer still opens by saying it cannot perform the comparison because the C.A.T.T.U.S evidence is absent.

MODEL SMOKE, run three times against the real repository with AUTO_PATCH_ENABLED=false; deepseek-harness verified 0 dirty before and after each run. Role balance alone produced an answer citing only documentation and manifests - 0 of 6 acquired source files named - because the acquired source did not answer the question. After obligation tokens, the same request produced 9 implementation-source citations across 5 of 6 acquired files (agent-loop/src/index.ts, agent.ts, invariant.ts; agent-default-model/src/index.ts, invariant.ts) alongside 6 documentation citations, and grounded a recommendation in invariant.ts rather than in prose. ANSWER.GROUND.LIVE.1/.2 refused the ungrounded names the model reached for in every run.

COST. Measured, not estimated: role classification plus role-balanced selection over a synthetic 4,002-path inventory takes 46.9 ms per call (20-call mean). On the real repository the whole acquisition prefix - selecting from 4,000 inventory paths and reading 12 files - takes 114 ms, against a 16-26 second repository inventory walk this phase does not touch. Pre-phase selection and reading was 19 ms; the delta is about +95 ms and buys 20,241 characters of relevant implementation source. No overall T5 latency improvement is claimed.

NOT MULTI-ROOT. This phase only fixes within-root starvation. The deepseek-harness side of the T5 comparison becomes deeper; the C.A.T.T.U.S side remains unavailable by design and the answer keeps saying so. Cross-root read authority needs its own contract and is not begun here.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS, measured. MAX_INVENTORY_SCAN still caps candidates at the first 4,000 inventory paths, which on deepseek-harness holds 1,360 of 2,700 TypeScript files - ample for a 12-file budget, but half the workspace is not considered. INPUT.1 truncates a long obligation at about 250 characters, so on the canonical T5 request the words tool, plugin, lifecycle, context and retrieval never reach token extraction and dimensions 2 and 3 of the question stay documentation-backed while dimension 1 became source-backed. Localized .zh.md duplicates can still take a documentation slot on other prompts.
phases.summary: Live analysis-capability fix for how the read-only route SPENDS its bounded evidence budget. WAITER.LIVE.1 gave the analysis route a fixed priority order over paths - user-named files, then a repository's own documents, then its manifests, then a fixed list of ROOT-LEVEL entry-point names, then any markdown under docs/. Replayed verbatim against the real deepseek-harness monorepo on the canonical T5 prompt, that order selected 12 files: 11 markdown documents (four of them Chinese translations of documents already selected) and 1 package.json, spending 59,674 of the 60,000 character budget on prose while 2,700 supported TypeScript files sat unread in the same inventory. The T5 architecture answer was accurate and shallow. Nothing was misconfigured: .ts is a supported extension, the files were inventoried, and the route was correct. Two measured causes: there was no evidence role that could hold code, so code could never be reserved; and the entry-point list was root-anchored, while a pnpm workspace keeps its entry points at packages/<name>/src/index.ts. ANALYSIS.EVIDENCE.LIVE.1 keeps every bound (12 files, 60,000 total characters, 6,000 per file) and divides the budget across deterministic evidence roles instead: implementation_source and test_example are added beside WAITER.LIVE.1's requested_path, project_document, package_manifest and requested_subject. A small evidence profile - architecture_implementation, implementation_detail, documentation_explanation, dependency_configuration or general_analysis - is derived by literal marker match from the obligations and subjects INPUT.1 already preserved, and states a per-role minimum. Reservation runs before fill and is interleaved, so each reserved role reaches the reader before the character budget can be exhausted; that ordering, not the reservation alone, is what makes source actually READ rather than merely selected. Path-matching tokens are drawn from the obligations as well as the subjects, which is what makes the acquired source the RIGHT source: the preserved subjects on the live T5 request are only (deepseek, harness) and reach UI settings dialogs and API plumbing, while the obligations carry agent, loop and extension and reach packages/core/agent-loop. Exactly requested paths are still taken first and are never displaced by a quota. Role detection reuses core.source_file_policy's SOURCE_ROLE_BY_EXTENSION and core.eligibility_policy's test/snapshot/temporary/historical location rules rather than adding a second extension map; tests, examples, archived material, build configuration, generated output and vendored copies are demoted rather than excluded, so none displaces primary implementation source while primary source exists. Measured afterwards on the identical prompt and repository: 6 implementation-source files and 20,241 TypeScript characters acquired - agent-loop/src/{index,agent,invariant,constants}.ts and agent-default-model/src/{index,invariant}.ts - alongside README.md, docs/architecture.md and the two owning package manifests, inside the same 12-file cap and well under the same character cap. A documentation question over an identical fixture still selects zero source files, which is what proves the profile depends on task semantics rather than on what the repository happens to contain. The phase adds no model call, no embedding, no network call, no repository traversal, no persisted index and no authority; multi-root access to ../C.A.T.T.U.S remains refused, and an architecture answer that could reach no source now says so instead of presenting documentation as implementation proof.

notes: PROVENANCE IS THE WHOLE GATE. A repository outside the active project root enters analysis evidence only because the USER named it as a subject of the task. extract_requested_root_literals reads the preserved obligations, ExplicitEvidence file paths and task subjects - already-frozen explicit input - and nothing else. A model draft saying 'I should also inspect ../third-repo', a README linking to another project and a source import pointing outside the root are all data, not authorization. Pinned by test_a_repository_only_the_model_mentioned_is_never_read, test_a_repository_a_document_links_to_is_never_read and test_a_repository_an_import_points_at_is_never_read.

'..' IS NOT THE DENIAL CRITERION. T5 legitimately writes ../C.A.T.T.U.S, so 'the string contains ..' cannot be the rule. '..' triggers CANDIDACY; acceptance requires resolution, project-root validation, identity derivation, duplicate collapse, the root-count cap and a bindable containment boundary, each with its own closed status. /etc/passwd is refused before the filesystem is touched, on the literal the user typed with any drive letter stripped, so the verdict is identical on Linux (where it exists and is a file) and on Windows (where it would canonicalize to C:/etc/passwd and merely not exist). A safety property must not rest on an accident of platform.

READ SCOPE IS A TYPE, NOT A FLAG. AnalysisReadScope exposes evidence_read_allowed True and write_authority, patch_application_authority, execution_authority, human_review_eligible and approval_ready False as read-only properties on a frozen dataclass, and AnalysisRepositorySubject.__post_init__ refuses to attach a scope to a root that is not accepted. Reusing a write-authority flag to mean 'read allowed' is unrepresentable rather than merely untested. Accepting Root B widens nothing: no patch candidate may be produced for it, and a later coding task must establish its own active project scope.

ALLOCATE, DO NOT MULTIPLY. The global budget stays 12 files / 60,000 characters / 6,000 per file across BOTH repositories. Exactly requested files are hoisted first in every root that has them - generic balancing never evicts a path the user named - and everything else is taken one file at a time, rotating between roots over each root's own role-balanced reading order, of which only a prefix is taken so the within-root reservation survives. Rotation makes the floor availability-aware without a quota (a small root contributes what it has and its unused slots are spent) and keeps the character budget symmetric, because the reading order IS the allocation order.

CONTAINMENT IS PER ROOT, AND SYMLINKS DO NOT WIDEN IT. Each accepted root gets its own boundary bound to its own canonical root; there is no shared largest-common-parent. A relative path belonging to root A never resolves through root B. Containment is checked on the canonical target - resolve() then relative_to() - so a link inside an approved repository that points outside it is refused: approving a repository never approved what its links reach. The secondary membership walk is core.repo_librarian._walk_policy_files, which already runs followlinks=False and drops symlinks resolving outside the root; no weaker rule was written for secondary roots.

TRAVERSAL, MEASURED AND NOT UNDERSTATED. This phase cannot claim traversal delta zero: a previously unreadable repository must obtain membership somehow. The claim it does make and measure is AT MOST ONE canonical membership traversal per newly accepted root per analysis request. Primary root: existing inventory reused, 0 additional walks. Refused root: 0 walks, not even a directory listing for a system path. Additional accepted root: exactly 1, through the same walker and the same ignore policy - measured 1,315 files in 2.19s against the primary's 6,126 files in 16.0s that production already builds. No ProgramGraph, no index, no embedding, no reparse, no second scan.

SYMBOL UNIVERSES STAY SEPARATE NOW THAT THERE ARE TWO. _state_repository_evidence emits one RepositoryEntityEvidence per accepted root and the primary fold skips items belonging to another repository, so a symbol defined only in root A cannot ground a claim about root B. Citations are rendered as repository::path, which is the reference grammar ANSWER.GROUND.LIVE.1 already parses rather than a new syntax invented here, and each excerpt carries a cite= line spelling the exact string. Two repositories holding the same src/index.ts produce two disambiguated entries, never one deduped by relative path.

PARTIAL COMPARISONS ARE STATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A requested root that cannot be resolved or read does not fail the analysis: the available root is analysed, the refused subject appears in [REPOSITORIES] with its status and reason and again as an evidence gap, and the prompt is told to report the comparison as partial rather than construct the missing half from the half it holds. The symmetric rule matters as much - where a repository WAS read the prompt says so and forbids opening with a claim of inaccessibility, because an answer that hedges about evidence it holds is as wrong as one that invents evidence it does not.

MEASURED ON THE EXACT LIVE T5 DETERMINISTIC PREFIX, no provider call, real repositories, primary inventory supplied as production supplies it: roots accepted 1 -> 2; deepseek-harness 12 files / 59,674 chars -> 6 files / 20,802 chars; C.A.T.T.U.S 0 / 0 -> 6 files / 17,604 chars; implementation source in the second root 0 -> 3 and project documents 0 -> 2; global files 12 -> 12, global chars 59,674 -> 38,406; root balance every_accepted_root_represented; unmet role requirements none in either root; membership traversals added 1; validation listings 1; model calls 1 draft / 0 review unchanged. Performance: root resolution 0.003s, primary membership reused 0.012s, secondary membership 2.19s, selection 0.076s, acquisition 0.004s, prefix total 2.28s.

COMPATIBILITY, PINNED NOT ASSUMED. Single-root analysis is byte-identical with and without the analysis_only gate - same selections, gaps, profile, selection reason and unmet requirements. A documentation-only task stays documentation-centric and a sibling repository that merely exists on disk changes nothing. Single-root evidence items carry no repository_id key at all, and a historical artifact with no multi-root receipt reports single_root_legacy - which is what it is, not a failed multi-root acquisition. T1/T2/T3/T4 never reach the multi-root path: it activates only on analysis_only, so defect_repair, explicit_change and needs_clarification stay inside the active project root regardless of what any text mentions.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS, measured. The second root grounds only what was actually read - no inventory is carried across - so a path that exists in root B but was not acquired stays unverified rather than confirmed; that is the conservative direction for a grounding gate and an acknowledged asymmetry with the primary root. A file path inside another root (../repo-b/src/x.ts) is classified as a requested FILE and does not by itself open repo-b; the user must name the repository. Root validation is conservative about system locations, so a genuine project under /usr/local/src would be refused. Within-root selection quality is unchanged and still imperfect: on the real T5 run C.A.T.T.U.S's sixth slot went to a benchmark fixture rather than production code, which is ANALYSIS.EVIDENCE.LIVE.1's ranking and deliberately not touched here. MAX_SUBJECT_TOKENS was not raised. Two roots is the cap; a three-way comparison returns explicit overflow evidence, not an answer. The symlink-escape test skips where the OS denies symlink creation, and the containment predicate it exercises is pinned separately on the real reader. Not report-only: this is the live analysis acquisition path.

Single-root analysis is byte-identical with and without the gate, historical artifacts report single_root_legacy rather than a failed multi-root acquisition, and T1/T2/T3/T4 never reach the multi-root path because it activates only on analysis_only. The phase adds no write, patch or execution authority, no model call, no network call, no index, no graph, no embedding and no routing change.

notes: THE MISSING LAYER, NAMED. The dogfood failure was not a bad threshold; it was an absent stage. The old router jumped from words to a mode, so a comparative architecture request with repository evidence needs fell into Instant Run. WAITER.1 inserts Task Shape and Capability Requirements between them and routes on capability predicates alone. No 0-100 complexity score, no weighted mode score, no Commander probability, no LLM confidence: every recommendation is a rule with a stable reason id and a sentence.

WORKFLOW IS NOT COMPUTE. WAITER.1 recommends one of four workflow classes: chat, instant_run, commander, project_evolution. It cannot name a provider, a model, a model size, cloud or local, a context window or a fallback chain, because no such field exists on any record it produces. A COMMANDER route means 'a workflow able to orchestrate several bounded operations', never 'use a bigger model'; a CHAT route never means 'use a small local model'. Regression tests render every routed decision, strip the authority block that names those powers in order to deny them, and assert that no compute token survives anywhere else.

THE ENTRY GATE FAILS CLOSED AND DOES NOT NEGOTIATE. Routing requires INPUT.3's derived ready_for_future_handoff: READY completion, an actual contract, a passed INPUT.1 preservation gate, and valid INPUT.2 receipt evidence. WAITER.1 re-derives it rather than trusting a flag and adds two integrity checks of its own - the supplied contract and decision must describe one run, and INPUT.1's own routing_allowed must be true. ASK_CLARIFICATION, GOAL_BRIEF_ASSIST, BLOCKED_CONTRADICTION, SEMANTIC_SYSTEM_FAILURE, a preservation failure, a missing or invalid semantic receipt, and a standalone preview all produce not_handoff_ready with no workflow, no shape and no capabilities. A blocked order is not described at all: WAITER.1 does not reinterpret it to rescue it and does not call a model.

WAITER DOES NOT REINTERPRET THE USER. No regex over prose for pronouns, comparisons, task type, complexity, project intent or repository need. Shape is derived from the task classification, the surviving relationships, the recorded execution requirements and INPUT.1's literal explicit evidence. The single place raw_request.text is touched is the literal substring check that backs a project-evolution declaration, which extracts no meaning and mirrors INPUT.1's preservation-gate identity comparison. The consequence is that the policy is language-independent by construction: an English explanation request and its Vietnamese equivalent produce byte-identical task shapes.

CAPABILITIES ARE REQUIREMENTS, NOT PERMISSIONS. repository_read_required=true says a future workflow would have to read the repository; it grants no repository_read_authority, opens no file, and records that WAITER.1 read nothing. Each required capability cites the structured facts it came from, drawn from a bounded vocabulary of INPUT field paths and Task Shape fields, so a derived requirement can never be phrased as something the user said. A test asserts the dogfood repository requirement cites task_contract.execution_requirements.repository_inspection_required and contains neither 'user' nor 'requested'.

COMPARISON DOES NOT CHOOSE A ROUTE; EVIDENCE SCOPE DOES. The strongest proof in the suite runs the identical DeepSeek dogfood prompt twice, changing only what INPUT recorded as needed. With repository inspection and multi-stage work it is broad_repository and routes COMMANDER; with everything supplied in the request it is direct_context and routes CHAT. Both carry analysis_shape=comparative and comparison_required=true. A bounded config change made 'based on that comparison' still routes INSTANT_RUN.

BROAD IS NOT ONGOING. The project_evolution family is unreachable by breadth, difficulty, file count, architecture or prompt length: TaskShape refuses to be constructed in that family without a verified declaration, and the declaration must be explicit and literally present in the preserved raw request. A whole-architecture refactor and a multi-component storage migration both route COMMANDER and carry the disqualifier project_evolution_not_explicitly_requested. A declaration the user never typed is refused and recorded as project_evolution_declaration_not_literally_supported.

KNOWN INPUT REPRESENTATION LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: INPUT.1's frozen task vocabulary has no value for project-evolution lifecycle intent, so WAITER.1 cannot read one off the contract. Rather than infer it from complexity, the declaration is an explicit optional input that defaults to absent and is verified against the user's own words. With no declaration supplied, PROJECT_EVOLUTION is simply never recommended. If a future INPUT phase learns to represent lifecycle intent structurally, it should fill this declaration; no INPUT.1-3 module was changed to accommodate it.

STATUS VOCABULARY IS THREE, AND WHY: routed, not_handoff_ready, uncertain. An 'unsupported' status was considered and deliberately not created - every capability in the bounded vocabulary is within reach of one of the four workflow classes, so the status could never be produced, and a status that cannot occur is decoration rather than honesty. 'uncertain' is real: a verified handoff whose family is unknown and whose capabilities demand nothing gets no recommendation, because guessing one would be the original failure in a new costume.

DETERMINISTIC BY CONSTRUCTION. No timestamp, no random id, no model output, no ambient machine state, no filesystem state and no network can affect a recommendation. The four modules import nothing beyond dataclasses, hashlib, json and typing; a static test asserts that none of them contains an os, subprocess, socket, requests, urllib or pathlib import or an open() call. Each decision fingerprints the exact contract and completion decision it consumed with sha256 over canonical JSON.

REPORT-ONLY AND UNWIRED. Nothing calls route_execution_workflow in a live path. Chat, Instant Run, Commander, Mixed Mode, the Unified Workbench, Project Evolution, Goal Brief, Dream, CTX.SELECT, the planner, the indexer, the graph, patching, validation, benchmarks, the model Driver and provider routing are all untouched, and no workflow starts because of a recommendation. Every decision serializes an authority block with routing execution, execution, repository read and write, patch, validation, benchmark, worker launch, provider selection, model selection, model escalation, dream, project evolution, planning and context selection authority all false, and human approval required true. recommended_workflow=project_evolution does not grant project_evolution_authority.

RECOMMENDING IS NOT PLANNING. When COMMANDER is recommended the decision stops at the workflow name. There is no stage list, no read set, no file list, no reconnaissance and no CTX.SELECT call - not fields WAITER.1 declines to fill, but fields it does not have. Recommended next phase is WAITER.2, which should take a routed recommendation under its own authority gate and decide how the selected workflow acquires its evidence.

PROJECT EVOLUTION PROVENANCE, CLOSED. Literal backing is necessary and not sufficient. A caller holding a real span of the user's prose can attach an invented label to it, so 'Do not use Project Evolution; just refactor this architecture' plus evidence_text='Project Evolution' would have routed an explicit refusal into the workflow it refused. check_project_evolution_request now applies four checks that must all pass: a declaration was supplied; declared_by names one of two trusted sources (explicit_input_evidence, human_declared_workflow_intent); source_raw_request_sha256 is this request's own INPUT.1 fingerprint; and evidence_text is a literal span of the preserved request that does not sit after the marker of a prohibition the user wrote. The untrusted source vocabulary (inferred, waiter_inference, model_inference, task_shape_inference, task_complexity, repository_scope) is representable so a caller's honest admission can be recorded and refused rather than laundered into a trusted value; none of the six can authorise anything. No INPUT.1-3 module was modified: raw_request.sha256 and ExplicitConstraint already existed.

A REFUSED DECLARATION DISQUALIFIES ONE WORKFLOW, NOT THE REQUEST. Every provenance failure leaves status=routed and lets the ordinary rule table pick commander, instant_run or chat, recording a stable disqualifier (project_evolution_not_explicitly_authorized, project_evolution_provenance_unverified, project_evolution_declaration_not_literally_supported, project_evolution_declaration_negated_by_user). WAITER.1 asks the user no clarification question. When no declaration was supplied at all the commander route still carries project_evolution_not_explicitly_requested; when one was supplied and refused, that code is replaced by the specific check it failed.
phases.summary: First Execution Waiter phase: a pure, deterministic layer that consumes a handoff-verified INPUT.3 CompletionDecision and its INPUT.1 Task Contract, derives a bounded Task Shape and bounded Capability Requirements from structured facts alone, and recommends one execution workflow class (chat, instant_run, commander, project_evolution) through an explicit rule table. It fails closed on any unverified handoff, never reinterprets the raw request, never plans, never reads the repository, never selects a provider or model, and grants zero authority.

notes: REQUIREMENT, NOT ACQUISITION. WAITER.2 answers 'what evidence does the selected workflow need?' and never 'go and obtain that evidence'. The contract states evidence domains, roles and tiers as classes. It contains no file, no path, no glob, no search query, no read set, no retrieval result, no repository manifest, no graph activation and no execution plan - not fields it declines to fill, but fields the record does not have. Regression tests render every specified contract and assert that no path fragment, no file extension, no query token and no host name survives anywhere in it.

DOMAIN IS NOT ROLE. The DeepSeek Harness dogfood considered roughly 6,087 repository files as one homogeneous bucket, including end-to-end tests, snapshots, rejected and proposed notes, and duplicate bilingual documentation. WAITER.2 separates where evidence comes from (direct_context, repository, validation_artifacts, historical_context, external_information) from how it may be used (supplied_material, implementation_authority, interface_contract, configuration_authority, architecture_description, validation_evidence, hypothesis_support, historical_context, current_external_authority). A test and a runtime module share a domain and must never share a role.

PRIORITY, NOT SWEEP. For broad repository reconnaissance the contract puts implementation authority, interface contracts, configuration authority and authoritative architecture description at required_primary; validation artifacts at required_secondary; historical material at deferred; and generated artifacts, snapshots and temporary artifacts at excluded_initially, with duplicate renderings and unrelated validation artifacts deferred. Tiers are deterministic; there is deliberately no 0-100 relevance score. A later retrieval layer may score inside a tier, never invent one.

TESTS ARE TASK-SENSITIVE, NOT GLOBALLY SECONDARY. Validation artifacts are secondary when they are the instrument of a survey and primary when they are its subject. The distinction is decided from INPUT.1's own preserved file paths and surviving subjects by a narrow lexical rule (a test/tests directory segment the user wrote, or a final segment starting test_ or containing _test.), never from prose and never from the filesystem. A differential regression pins both halves: the same repository, one order about architecture and one about a failing test, produce opposite tiers.

HISTORY EXPLAINS, IT DOES NOT TESTIFY. Proposed, rejected and superseded material is required at the deferred tier with the role historical_context, and never carries current_authority. The contract additionally emits the verification requirement current_implementation_outranks_historical_material. A later verifier may promote a historical claim; nothing in this phase can.

GENERATED AND SNAPSHOT MATERIAL IS CATEGORY-LEVEL POLICY. Generated output, snapshots, scratch artifacts and duplicated renderings are stated as deferred or excluded source classes. No ignore file is read, no directory is walked, and no member of any class is ever named or discovered.

NO CAPABILITY ESCALATION. Every evidence domain names the upstream capability that licenses it: repository, validation_artifacts and historical_context are all licensed by repository_read_required, since all three are repository-resident and requiring them restates a capability WAITER.1 already recorded; external_information is licensed by external_information_required; direct_context needs no licence because it is already in hand. A requirement outside the envelope fails the whole contract closed with capability_envelope_widened rather than widening scope quietly.

NO WORKFLOW ESCALATION, PROVED STRUCTURALLY. The layer that derives the requirements (core/evidence_policy.py) is never given the selected workflow, so no evidence need can argue for a different route; the orchestrator copies recommended_workflow verbatim. Chat is never promoted to Commander, Instant Run never to Commander, Commander never to Project Evolution. A static test asserts the policy module contains no router symbol at all.

FAIL CLOSED ON ANYTHING THAT DOES NOT HANG TOGETHER. A WAITER.1 status other than routed produces not_routed with no requirements. A supplied contract or completion decision that does not fingerprint to the ones the routing decision was made over produces inconsistent_input. So does an unsupported workflow and an envelope violation. WAITER.2 never re-routes, never reinterprets the raw prompt, and never describes an order nobody routed.

NO MODEL, NO PROVIDER, NO COMPUTE. The record has no field for a provider, a model, local or cloud, a context window, a temperature or a fallback chain. Evidence source is not compute choice. Regression tests render every contract, strip the authority block that names those powers in order to deny them, and assert that no compute token survives anywhere else.

ZERO ACQUISITION AUTHORITY. repository_read_authority, repository_write_authority, external_search_authority, context_selection_authority, indexing_authority, graph_authority, retrieval_authority, execution_authority, patch_authority, validation_authority, worker_launch_authority, provider_selection_authority, model_selection_authority, planning_authority, routing_authority and project_evolution_authority are all false in every status, including a fully specified one. human_approval_required is true. A required evidence domain grants nothing.

DETERMINISM. The same routed decision over the same upstream records always produces the same contract, on any machine, at any time, with any repository state and no network. The modules import no os, subprocess, socket, requests, urllib, pathlib, random or time, and open no file. An English broad-analysis order and its Vietnamese equivalent produce byte-identical evidence contracts, because none of the derivation reads words.

REPORT-ONLY AND UNWIRED. Nothing calls derive_evidence_requirements in a live path. CTX.SELECT, the Canonical Graph, the Activation Graph, the indexer, the repository manifest, web search, the planner, Instant Run, Commander, Project Evolution, Dream, the Workbench and Mixed Mode are all untouched, and a test walks the repository sources to assert no caller exists outside the tests. INPUT.1-3 and WAITER.1 modules were not modified; WAITER.2 is built entirely around their public contracts.

NO REQUIRED-CAPABILITY LOSS. The licence table read the other way is a closure rule: every capability WAITER.1 requires names the evidence domain and role that discharge it, and a contract carrying none of them at an active tier fails closed with required_capability_dropped. Deferred material does not discharge an obligation - it is on the record and out of the work. Together with the envelope check the pair is what faithful means: not wider, and not narrower where evidence is required. CAPABILITY_EVIDENCE_OBLIGATIONS is total over CAPABILITY_NAMES and checked at import, so a capability added upstream cannot slip through by never being considered.

EXTERNAL EVIDENCE IS NEVER REDUCED TO DIRECT CONTEXT. A simple current-fact lookup stays on the CHAT route and keeps an external_information requirement at required_primary with an external-currency verification rule; external evidence is a source, not a workflow class, and never escalates chat to commander. An order that carries its own material and also needs a current external fact reaches both, and WAITER.2 reports mixed_sources rather than external_only - a label that would have contradicted its own required-primary supplied_material requirement. WAITER.1 was not modified: the refinement is read from the preserved contract WAITER.2 already holds, reaches no repository scope, and cannot widen the work.

RECOMMENDED NEXT PHASE. WAITER.3 or an ACQUIRE track should translate one Evidence Requirement Contract into bounded acquisition requests under its own authority gate - mapping domains and roles onto concrete sources, honouring the tiers and the deferrals, and obtaining nothing that the contract did not license.
phases.summary: Second Execution Waiter phase: a pure, deterministic layer that consumes one routed WAITER.1 decision together with the frozen INPUT records it was made over, and states what evidence the selected workflow will eventually need. It answers 'what ingredients should that kitchen request?' and never 'go and obtain them'. The Evidence Requirement Contract names bounded evidence domains (where evidence comes from), roles (how it may be used), priority tiers, a bounded scope, category-level deferrals and exclusions, and verification requirements - and contains no file, path, query, read set, retrieval result, repository manifest, graph activation or plan. It fails closed when WAITER.1 did not route, when the supplied contract and completion decision do not fingerprint to the ones the routing decision was made over, or when a derived requirement falls outside the upstream capability envelope. Report-only, unwired, and holding no acquisition authority of any kind.
phases.title: Deterministic Evidence Requirement Contract
