notes: Production failure and old path. Two black-box field tests, one cause: the live runtime had no place to say what kind of order it was holding before it started looking for something to patch. 'Compare deepseek-harness and C.A.T.T.U.S architecture' indexed for about 26 minutes, ranked an unrelated test file first, demanded an exact source_snippet and finished on the patch fallback prompt whose summary reads 'Cannot safely generate patch because CONTROL did not provide an exact source snippet', with the final answer echoing the user's own task. 'Add task priority support' produced a correct five-operation multi-file plan that enforce_control_grounding_on_payload then nulled, because a feature has no failing test and CONTROL.SAFETY.LIVE.1 correctly refuses to invent one.

New routing boundary. safe_route_live_task runs at the top of web.runner.run_agent_web, cli.interactive.create_agent_state and web.app._run_mode's default retrieve shell, before index_repository, before run_preflight_validation and before run_control_structured. Task classification now happens before the graph work that only a patch task needs.

Task shape vocabulary, four values and no more: analysis_only, defect_repair, explicit_change, needs_clarification. Precedence is fixed: empty request to clarification; an analysis obligation and a change obligation in separate ordered clauses to clarification; a defect claim to defect_repair; an explicit change request to explicit_change; an analysis marker or an INPUT.1 answer task type to analysis_only; anything else to clarification.

WAITER.1 reuse. derive_task_shape, derive_capability_requirements, select_workflow, waiter_authority and waiter_guardrails are consumed unchanged; INPUT.1's extract_explicit_evidence, ExplicitEvidenceInterpreter, check_requirement_preservation and understand_request are consumed unchanged. LiveTaskFieldsInterpreter wraps rather than replaces the deterministic interpreter and overrides exactly two fields it cannot derive: the task classification (no rule yields implementation or debugging, because INPUT.2's model was meant to and is not live) and the execution requirements (production already knows whether a repository is attached). Every product is labelled 'live compatibility adapter', not an authoritative semantic replacement.

Documented integration incompatibility. core.execution_waiter.route_execution_workflow consumes an INPUT.3 CompletionDecision, and core.waiter_receipt.check_handoff_eligibility rejects one whose INPUT.2 semantic receipt does not attest to model_call_count >= 1. INPUT.2 is not live, so the frozen entry point cannot be reached without adding the model call this phase forbids. The handoff gate, and only the handoff gate, is replaced, by INPUT.1's own fail-closed preservation verdict.

Change need versus defect versus authority. change_need_source has four values and no confidence: none, explicit_user_request, grounded_defect, unresolved. LiveTaskShape refuses to construct a shape claiming grounded_defect; only CONTROL.SAFETY.LIVE.1, from OPS.VALIDATE.1 evidence bound to exact source, may set it. A feature is change_requested=true with defect_established=false; an analysis question is false and false; a grounded bug is true and true. write_authority=false and patch_application_authority=false are read-only properties on every route in every shape.

Analysis path. Never enters patch localization, never requires a replacement snippet, never runs validation to answer a question, never indexes to classify, never gains write authority, and skips both maybe_run_auto_patch and the patch post-processing battery. Evidence is bounded document acquisition over the inventory production had already built (user-named paths, project documents, subject-matching paths, manifests, entry points, architecture docs), capped at 12 files / 6000 chars each / 60000 total, with gaps reported rather than hidden.

Explicit-change path. enforce_control_grounding_on_payload gains a second legitimate reason to pass: the user asked, and every proposed operation targets a file whose source this run actually acquired. Quote grounding, patch safety, CTX.PATCH/CTX.APPLY, forbidden paths, byte fidelity, validation and human approval are untouched, and build_patch_policy still requires defect_grounded for auto_apply_allowed, so an explicitly requested feature produces a reviewable plan and never an automatic write. Bounded multi-file plans stay available within the existing budgets.

Boundaries. Zero added model calls, network calls, index builds or graph traversals: routing reads only the words the user typed, and the analysis route removes indexing, preflight, CONTROL and Scout from that path. CONTROL.SAFETY.LIVE.1 guarantees are unweakened, so rank still cannot mint a defect, a false bug report still gets no patch eligibility, and inconclusive validation still establishes nothing. OPS.VALIDATE.1 semantics, OPS.PATCH.1, patch safety and CTX are unchanged. An unrouted CONTROL call (Dream, the proposal queue, web mode=control) behaves exactly as before.

Deliberately out of scope and recorded for later: retrieval and large-graph ranking quality for the defect route (CONTROL.SAFETY.LIVE.1 makes poor ranking safe; future work makes it useful), code_dna indentation, Phantom Limb, the CLI validation-directive UX, the DB-disabled create_session fallback, Commander decomposition for genuinely mixed orders, WORKER.DECL.2B (parked, untouched) and CHECK.2 / CHECK.3 / CHECK.LIVE.2A (not promoted).
phases.summary: Live production routing fix separating ANALYSIS, DEFECT_REPAIR and EXPLICIT_CHANGE deterministically before patch-localization CONTROL. WAITER.1's frozen Task Shape, Capability Requirement and workflow-policy derivations are consumed live through a small labelled compatibility adapter over INPUT.1's literal evidence extractor, deterministic interpreter and preservation gate; the one proven incompatibility is documented rather than worked around, because INPUT.3's handoff receipt requires evidence of an INPUT.2 semantic model call the live runtime cannot produce without adding one. An analysis-only order never indexes, never runs validation, never enters CONTROL, never requires a replacement snippet and never acquires write authority; it answers from bounded document evidence instead. A defect claim keeps the proven preflight/OPS.VALIDATE.1/CONTROL grounding path unchanged. An explicit change request establishes change_need_source=explicit_user_request from the user's preserved words without pretending a defect exists, and still requires acquired exact source, verbatim quotes, patch safety, CTX and existing authorization before any write. change_requested, defect_established and write_authority stay three separate facts; AUTO_PATCH_ENABLED, CTX.PATCH/CTX.APPLY and human approval remain monotonic. Ambiguous and mixed orders fail closed to a read-only clarification that preserves every obligation in order. No model call, network call, index build or graph traversal was added by routing, no retrieval redesign was attempted, no checker was promoted, and this is not report-only.

notes: OUTCOME IS WORKER_DECL_1_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, AND THAT IS A RESULT. No independent structured worker change declaration exists in this repository, pre-execution or post-execution, that could be wired without changing the worker prompt/response contract. Per the phase brief a precheck stop is a valid successful completion: the architecture's missing observation point is named, not papered over. No production module was modified and the CHECK.LIVE.1B seam is byte-identical.

THE QUALIFICATION IS EXECUTABLE, NOT NARRATIVE. tests/test_native_worker_declaration_qualification.py pins the four load-bearing facts: no response contract carries a declaration field, every model invocation precedes patch application, no production caller passes worker_declaration, and a real live run reports legacy_plan_derived. Two of the tests were checked to fail against a deliberately violating module before it was removed.

TIMING IS PROVENANCE. The last model turn on every instrumented apply path happens strictly before apply, verified by a transitive name-based call graph over core, agents, patching, web and scripts. The one post-application model turn, core/self_correct_loop.py, requests a replacement patch rather than a report, uses the same declaration-free response schema, and drives core.executor.Executor instead of run_patch_plan_with_artifacts; the patch-plan branch that does reach the instrumented boundary returns before that loop can start.

THE NEAR MISS IS RECORDED SO IT CANNOT BE MISTAKEN LATER. The dream planning pass emits a structured likely_files list from an already-existing separate model call, but it asks which files are relevant in a pass whose own prompt forbids writing a patch, and it arrives through prose JSON extraction. Reading intent out of it would infer a declaration from a field name, so it is pinned as a relevance hypothesis rather than quietly wired.

NO MANUFACTURED SOURCE AND NO SILENT WIDENING. Nothing is derived from PatchPlan operations or paths, ExecutionAuthorization, ObservedPostRunFacts, git diff, the side-effect collector or final filesystem state. The parsed model response reaches the run lifecycle only as the opaque control_result replay artifact and is never passed to LiveExecutionObservation. No prose parser, regular expression, model call, validation execution, repository traversal or network call was added, and patch application, order and payload are unchanged.

MEASURABILITY STAYS HONEST. Self-report fidelity and intent fidelity are both unmeasurable under this outcome, and the shadow receipt serialises no truthy fidelity claim, confidence value, trust score or worker-honesty score for a legacy plan-derived record. All CHECK results remain shadow-only; authoritative_effect remains a constant false property no caller can set.

A FUTURE PRODUCER MUST FIX THE STAGE VOCABULARY FIRST. core/live_worker_declaration.py accepts only declaration_stage=completed and serialises the stage-free value independent_worker_declaration. Because this architecture's last model turn is pre-application, the first realistic producer would be a pre-execution intent that today's contract would force to be labelled a completion. A pre_execution_intent stage, staged provenance values and derived read-only measurability flags must land before any producer is wired.

RECOMMENDED NEXT PHASE IS WORKER.DECL.2. Add a declared_changes field beside patch_plan in the patch response contract, add the pre-execution intent stage and staged provenance, and wire it through the existing CHECK.LIVE.1B seam. Such a field is an independently_declared_channel measuring internal output consistency, never independent evidence, and that distinction must not leak into EVIDENCE.2 independence semantics.
phases.summary: Report-only qualification of whether the real worker/runtime already produces an independent structured declaration of intended or completed changes that could be wired through the CHECK.LIVE.1B seam without adding a model invocation. The traced answer is no: every patch response contract in production (core/prompter.py, core/control_engine.py, patching/patch_gates.py, scripts/run_patch_proposal_queue.py) carries only summary, issues, patch_candidate, patch_plan, confidence and needs_escalation, with no field declaring changed paths apart from the executable operations themselves; worker_run.json is a subprocess process record; proposal.md and completion notes are prose; and the nearest structured candidate, the dream planning pass likely_files list, is a relevance hypothesis reached through JSON extraction from free-form model prose. The last model invocation precedes patch application on every instrumented apply path, no worker survives the apply boundary, and the one post-application model turn drafts a replacement patch on the separate Executor engine rather than reporting on a completed one. The phase therefore completes as WORKER_DECL_1_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE with no production module modified: ordinary runs keep reporting legacy_plan_derived honestly, no declaration is manufactured from patch-plan paths or observed filesystem facts, no prose is parsed, and no model call, validation execution, repository traversal, network call or patch behaviour is added. It promotes no checker, widens no authority, touches no frozen CHECK.1 or CHECK.2 module, and does not begin CHECK.LIVE.2.
phases.title: Native Worker Declaration Source Qualification & Wiring

notes: A PROTOCOL, NOT A SECOND HEURISTIC READER. The strict parser accepts a response only when json.loads of the entire stripped text yields one object. There is no re import, no fenced-block reader, no balanced-brace scanner, no first-object search and no Markdown cleanup, and the boundary suite asserts each absence. The one decoder entry point that could recover a prefix, raw_decode, appears exactly once inside a helper whose every return is a bounded status name, so no value decoded there can become an envelope.

THE EXPECTED DIVERGENCE IS THE MEASUREMENT. A fenced response, a prose preamble, trailing commentary and two concatenated objects are all rejected as surrounding_prose_rejected even where the legacy extractor recovers them. That is the point of the phase and not a defect: it is how often current provider output already conforms that WORKER.DECL.2B needs to know before it puts a typed field in this channel.

ONE RESPONSE, TWO PARSERS, ZERO EXTRA MODEL CALLS. The compatibility record is computed from the response the run already has and the legacy payload it already produced, at the three producer sites that hold both. Nothing is re-requested, re-formatted or repaired by a model; a repair turn would hide the very provider compatibility problem this phase exists to measure.

SEMANTIC IDENTITY, NOT STRING EQUALITY. Agreement is compared through a canonical patch-plan identity that mirrors what the executor acts on: operation order is significant because operations apply sequentially and replace_snippet rewrites only the first occurrence; the relative_path and file aliases resolve to one identity in the executor's own precedence; JSON key order and insignificant whitespace cannot change the fingerprint; and no clock, latency or provider response id enters it.

REJECT WHOLE, NEVER TRUNCATE. An oversized response, operation list, path or payload invalidates the entire envelope. A silently shortened operation list or snippet would change what a patch means, so the parser contains no slice of its input and no truncation helper, asserted statically. The operation ceiling is deliberately equal to CHECK.1's MAX_DECLARED_CHANGES and pinned by a test rather than by an import, keeping the worker protocol free of a checker dependency.

AUTHORITY CANNOT ENTER THROUGH THE ENVELOPE. write_authority, write_allowed, reviewer_approved, human_approved, merge_allowed, validation_passed and their siblings are rejected by name at both the envelope and operation levels rather than ignored as harmless metadata, and no allow-listed key name contains an authority, approval or merge word. Patch authorization remains exactly where it already lives.

SHADOW ONLY, AND THE PATCH IS UNTOUCHED. The lifecycle argument defaults to None, the persistence branch is guarded by a default-off flag, and only an already-typed record is written; a raw mapping is never laundered into one. With the flag on, applied operations, their order, the diffs, the rollback state, the worktree and the result key set are all identical to a run with it off, and a recorded strict_legacy_semantic_mismatch still applies exactly the caller's plan.

THE RECORD IS IDENTITY, NOT PAYLOAD. The additive worker_patch_envelope.json artifact in the existing replay bundle carries statuses, provenance, plan identities, an envelope fingerprint and bounded rejected key names. No snippet, file body, prompt or raw model response is duplicated into it, and an older bundle without the file stays readable.

NO CHANGE INTENT YET, ON PURPOSE. declared_changes and every sibling name are rejected as unknown fields, and worker_metadata is deliberately absent from the allow-list because WORKER.DECL.1 found no genuinely structured worker metadata to carry. WORKER.DECL.2B owns the first real added field, once this envelope is shown to survive the real provider path.

NO PROMPT CHANGE IN THIS PHASE. Section 19 permits testing a minimal instruction asking the same model call for exactly one JSON object, but measuring first and changing the request second keeps the transport-format experiment isolated. The repository already has the wording pattern in SCOUT_PROMPT, so a follow-up can apply it to the patch contract without redesigning patch instructions, reasoning strategy, temperature or provider.
phases.summary: Strict, bounded, one-object worker patch-response envelope, wired as a default-off shadow measurement beside the existing legacy channel. WORKER.DECL.1 found every patch-producing worker response transported as free-form text and recovered by extract_json_block, which regex-matches Markdown fences and then scans for balanced braces inside arbitrary prose; a channel like that cannot carry a trustworthy typed field. WorkerPatchEnvelope replaces the heuristic with a protocol: the entire non-whitespace response must decode as exactly one JSON object, its top-level keys are the allow-list schema_version and patch_plan, its operations reuse the existing create_file/replace_snippet contract unchanged with per-operation key allow-lists, and every bound is finite and rejects whole rather than truncating. Unknown and authority-shaped keys are refused by name, so a model cannot assert a write, approval, validation, routing or merge decision through this channel. Parse outcomes are the bounded statuses valid, invalid_json, non_object, unknown_field, schema_invalid, bound_exceeded, surrounding_prose_rejected and unsupported_schema_version, with no score or confidence anywhere. Each already-received response is read once by both parsers and recorded as strict_worker_patch_envelope, legacy_extracted_json or no_patch_payload plus a semantic agreement compared through canonical patch-plan identity, never string equality; a strict_legacy_semantic_mismatch is recorded and never resolved. The legacy payload stays authoritative throughout: the phase adds no model call, no output repair turn, no prompt change, no provider SDK, no validation execution, no repository traversal and no network call, changes no patch operation, order or payload, promotes no checker, and adds no change-intent field, which WORKER.DECL.2B owns.
phases.title: Strict Structured Patch Response Envelope

notes: THE REQUEST IS THE EXPERIMENTAL VARIABLE, AND THE ONLY ONE. Model identity, temperature, task content, patch operation schema, patch selection rules, safety instructions, authorization, validation and the execution lifecycle are all held fixed. The delta is a block appended after the existing patch contract, plus at most one provider media-type keyword on the request that was already going to be made.

FLAG OFF IS ARGUMENT-IDENTICAL, NOT MERELY EQUIVALENT. The off path returns the very same prompt object and an empty keyword mapping, so the client is invoked with exactly the arguments this repository has always used rather than with a new argument set to None. Existing test fakes pinned to the old signature keep working, which is the compatibility claim proving itself.

THE PARSER IS NOT WEAKENED TO RAISE THE NUMBER. WORKER.DECL.2A's parser is imported unchanged and this module defines no parse status of its own, imports no re, no json, and no legacy extractor, and contains no fence reader or brace scanner. A fenced or prose-wrapped response is still surrounding_prose_rejected even when the strict request asked for neither, and that rejection is the measurement.

NO SECOND CALL AND NO REPAIR TURN. A strict rejection never re-requests, reformats, verifies or retries: the boundary suite asserts one model call per generator function and that no producer site branches on a strict status. A repair turn would hide the very provider compatibility problem this experiment exists to measure.

PATCH SEMANTICS DECIDE ELIGIBILITY, NOT THE OTHER WAY AROUND. The envelope carries a patch_plan and nothing else, so the block is appended only where a plan is already the declared shape. Under safe_minimal a plan is forbidden and under balanced a patch_candidate is preferred; both keep the legacy request and are recorded honestly as legacy_prompt rather than being quietly enrolled.

LEGACY EXTRACTION REMAINS AUTHORITATIVE THROUGHOUT. Both parsers read the one response the run already has, the legacy payload is what the executor receives, a strict/legacy mismatch is recorded and never resolved, and a valid strict parse beside an absent legacy plan does not promote itself. The observation forces authoritative_effect to False structurally.

TRANSPORT PROVENANCE CARRIES NO RANK. provider_native_json is not stronger evidence than strict_prompt; it says how the same one-object request was expressed on the wire. A provider with no native mode keeps the prompt-only arm rather than losing the experiment, and no provider is given weaker envelope semantics. Core imports no provider SDK, and the provider adapter imports no core contract.

NO THRESHOLD YET, ON PURPOSE. The dogfood summary counts strict_valid, legacy_only, invalid_both and semantic_mismatch by provider family and by transport strategy, and contains no rate, percentage, threshold, score, confidence or verdict. A human reads the distribution and decides whether adoption is good enough for WORKER.DECL.2B; nothing in the code branches on it.

NO CHANGE INTENT, NO CHECKER PROMOTION. change_intent, declared_changes and any pre-execution intent field remain outside the contract and are still rejected as unknown_field, which WORKER.DECL.2B will change. CHECK.1, CHECK.2, CHECK.LIVE.1 and CHECK.LIVE.1B are untouched, unimported and unpromoted, and no model JSON can assert a write, approval, validation or merge decision through this channel.

THE BASELINE COSTS NO MODEL CALL. Current provider behaviour is measured offline from recorded artifacts an operator names, classified by the frozen parser with a legacy-derived shape label that explains a rejection but can never undo one. The tool lives outside every run path and performs no model call and no network call.
phases.summary: Opt-in experiment that changes the request behind WORKER.DECL.2A's frozen strict envelope and measures whether real providers will emit it. WORKER.DECL.2A wired the strict one-object parser in shadow and found the expected answer, surrounding_prose_rejected, because nothing had asked the model for anything else: only the reader had changed. This phase changes the output-format request on already-scheduled patch-generation calls and nothing else. One flag, STRICT_WORKER_PATCH_ENVELOPE_EMISSION, defaults off and off is a no-op: the prompt is the identical object, the provider call is argument-identical, and no artifact is written. On, it appends a transport block reusing SCOUT_PROMPT's own strict-output wording, and may attach a provider's native JSON media type to that same request, under a bounded transport vocabulary of legacy_prompt, strict_prompt and provider_native_json. Transport is provenance, never epistemic strength, and every arm is judged by the same frozen parser, which is not weakened: a fenced, prose-wrapped, unknown-field or authority-shaped response is still rejected, and change_intent is still unknown_field. The strict block is appended only where the site's existing patch contract already declares a patch_plan as the shape wanted, so no patch rule, operation schema or safety instruction is overridden; the dream site, whose prompt resolves to safe_minimal, is deliberately left on the legacy request. The legacy extractor stays the authoritative source of every applied patch plan: a strict rejection cannot fail a run, select a plan or reach the executor, and it never triggers a retry. Model calls, network requests, validation executions and repository traversals are all unchanged at zero delta, no checker is promoted, no threshold is defined, and a bounded emission observation of statuses, provider family, transport strategy and an envelope fingerprint is the only new record. Adoption counts are reported for a human to read; nothing branches on them.
phases.title: Strict Envelope Emission Adoption Experiment
validation: python -m compileall core scripts agents tests

notes: OBSERVATION ONLY, AND IT SHOWS IN THE DIFF. This phase adds no production field, no production file and no production test; allowed_files is a design document, the registry and the two registration test files. WORKER.DECL.2A.1 is used exactly as frozen, and the operator harness that drove it lived outside the repository so that not even a scripts/ helper could drift into a run path.

THE FIRST PHASE THAT DECLARES A MODEL CALL. Every one of the 138 phases before it was local_only with model_calls_allowed false. This one is strong_model_requires_approval with model_calls_allowed true, which is the only combination core/phase_registry.py permits for a phase that spends provider calls. network_allowed stays false because the validator rejects true outright for ROAD.1-managed phases; the registry vocabulary expresses provider traffic through model_calls_allowed alone, and the design document says so rather than letting the flag read as no traffic at all.

ONE CALL PER RUN, PROVEN AT THE BOUNDARY. A pass-through counter on the provider SDK recorded exactly one generate_content per run in all five runs, in the control arm and both experimental arms alike. Strict checking added no formatting turn, no repair turn, no verifier turn and no retry, and no run branched on a strict status. The pre-existing reviewer-model fallback loop can attempt a second model when the first errors, which is not caused by strict checking and did not fire in any live run.

THE OBSERVATION IS TIED TO THE RESPONSE IT DESCRIBES. For every run the sha256 of the recorded raw_model_response equals the sha256 of the text the provider boundary returned, the observation the production site handed the lifecycle is byte-identical to the observation recomputed from that exact text with the frozen functions, and the replay bundle carries strict_envelope_emission.json in precisely the four flag-on runs. No fixture result is reported as live.

TRANSPORT WAS ISOLATED, NOT CONFOUNDED. strict_prompt and provider_native_json sent a byte-identical prompt on the same case, differing only by response_mime_type application/json on the request. That makes the two arms a clean transport comparison and also means native JSON was never tested without the strict block, so this phase cannot say whether the media type alone would suffice.

LEGACY STAYED AUTHORITATIVE WITH A VALID STRICT PARSE IN HAND. All four experimental runs parsed valid, and in none of them did the strict result select, alter or apply anything: the legacy extractor read the same object, produced the plan, applied one operation, performed no rollback and validated. Authority did not move because a strict parse succeeded, which is the case the guardrail existed for.

PATCH QUALITY IS OUT OF SCOPE AND STAYS THERE. validation_ok was true in all five runs and that is reported as execution context only. Five runs on two cases and one model are not a controlled patch-quality A/B, no rate or percentage is published, and nothing in the code branches on the distribution.

NO CHANGE INTENT, NO PARSER RELAXATION, NO PROMOTION. The two-field envelope survived live production unchanged, which is what WORKER.DECL.2B was waiting on; change_intent and declared_changes are still unknown_field, core/worker_patch_envelope.py is untouched and forbidden, CHECK.1, CHECK.2, CHECK.LIVE.1 and CHECK.LIVE.1B are unimported and unpromoted, and no runtime routing was derived from case A.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT COVER. One provider family, one model, one enrolled site, two cases, five runs. The pipeline site still needs a vibe style, the dream site still carries the pre-existing safe_minimal contradiction, ollama and deepseek remain proven by test rather than by traffic, and patch_candidate-only responses stay invisible to the envelope. A wider adoption picture needs runs this phase deliberately did not manufacture.
phases.summary: Operator-approved live dogfood that replaces WORKER.DECL.2A.1's 'live observations = 0' with real provider evidence for the strict emission channel, changing no production code and no production test. Five runs of the unconditionally enrolled patch-producing site, scripts/run_patch_proposal_queue.py, were driven through its own main() against google gemma-4-31b-it at temperature 0.0 over two benchmark cases in disposable temp repositories: one legacy_prompt control, two strict_prompt runs and two provider_native_json runs. The control returned a fenced four-key payload and was surrounding_prose_rejected; all four experimental runs returned a bare two-key object whose first character was { and last was }, parsed valid by the frozen WORKER.DECL.2A parser with agreement agreed and a distinct envelope fingerprint each. Every run made exactly one provider call, so additional calls caused by strict checking is zero; legacy extraction stayed authoritative and applied one operation per run with no rollback and validation_ok true in all five. The chain was proven rather than asserted: the sha256 of each recorded raw_model_response equals the sha256 of the response the provider boundary returned, the in-run observation equals the observation recomputed from that exact text, and strict_envelope_emission.json appears in the replay bundle of exactly the four enabled runs and not of the control. The two experimental arms sent a byte-identical prompt, differing only by response_mime_type application/json on the wire, so the comparison isolates transport. Classified as case A, strict channel empirically demonstrated, on a single model and a single site; no threshold, rate or routing policy is derived from it, no parser is relaxed, no checker is promoted, and pre_execution_change_intent is still rejected as unknown_field.
phases.title: Live Strict Envelope Adoption Dogfood
validation: python -m compileall core scripts agents tests

notes: ONE INVOCATION, TWO STRUCTURED CHANNELS. The v2 strict prompt asks the already-scheduled call for patch_plan and change_intent together. The added model-call and network-call counts are both zero. The provider-native arm reuses application/json and introduces no response-schema experiment.

STRUCTURAL SEPARATION IS NOT EVIDENTIAL INDEPENDENCE. independently_declared_channel means software did not derive intent from operations. It never means independent evidence, corroboration or lineage, because the same model response emitted both siblings.

V1 MEANING IS FROZEN. parse_strict_worker_patch_envelope still accepts only the historical two-key v1 object and still rejects change_intent. parse_strict_worker_patch_envelope_v2 requires the additive field under a new schema identifier; old artifacts are not rewritten or silently reinterpreted.

INTENT IS PRE-EXECUTION, NEVER COMPLETION. Native v2 declarations carry declaration_stage=pre_execution_intent and source_provenance=pre_execution_worker_intent. The frozen CHECK.1 status slot receives partial as an adapter marker, while live metadata explicitly interprets declared_but_unobserved as intended_change_not_materialized rather than a completion overclaim.

DISAGREEMENT IS DATA. Intent and plan may have different path sets or kinds and the envelope remains valid. Intent and objective final changes may likewise differ. Separate bounded diagnostics preserve agreed, missing, extra, kind-mismatch, mixed and unavailable relations without repair or retry.

AUTHORITY NEVER FLOWS FROM INTENT. Patch safety and ExecutionAuthorization remain based on the caller-supplied executable plan. Intent is never unioned with that plan, cannot make a path writable, cannot change an operation and cannot affect the authoritative result even when CHECK.1 is suspicious or blocked in shadow.

LEGACY IS STILL AUTHORITATIVE. Strict v2 parsing only freezes native intent telemetry. The existing legacy extractor supplies the plan to the executor. A malformed or missing intent produces native intent unavailable and a legacy_plan_derived declaration source where compatible; it does not fail the run or synthesize intent from plan paths.

BOUNDED DURABLE DOGFOOD. The proposal queue exports pre_execution_change_intent.json into its established .agent/proposals item directory before the disposable clone is deleted. The receipt contains no raw response, prompt, snippets, file bodies, environment values or credentials, and the temporary repository lifetime is unchanged.

CHECK.1 REMAINS FROZEN AND SHADOW-ONLY. The existing CHECK.LIVE.1B adapter is reused; live metadata carries stage and intent-specific interpretations. CHECK.2 and CHECK.3 are not invoked, no checker is authoritative, no severity/honesty/confidence score exists, and counts decide nothing.

LIVE STOP CONDITION NOT YET MET. Offline implementation and validation are complete. The bounded strict_prompt production run used one existing Google generation with no fallback, retained a successful authoritative legacy apply/validation and a reconciled shadow CHECK.1 result, but v2 was surrounding_prose_rejected and native intent was unavailable. The provider_native_json process was not started because its host network escalation was denied. No percentage or transport conclusion is claimed, and the phase remains active until real v2-valid intent plus plan is preserved on the production path.
phases.summary: Default-off, shadow-only additive v2 evolution of WorkerPatchEnvelope. The same already-scheduled strict worker invocation emits patch_plan and change_intent as separate sibling fields; software never derives intent from operations, prose, legacy extraction or observed filesystem changes. V1 remains frozen and loadable under worker_decl_2a_patch_envelope_v1, while worker_decl_2b_patch_envelope_v2 requires the bounded immutable pre_execution_intent structure with explicit added/modified repository-relative paths. The accepted intent is frozen before apply, adapted to WorkerChangeDeclaration with pre_execution_worker_intent provenance and independently_declared_channel lineage, then passed through the existing CHECK.LIVE.1B WorkerReport seam. Same-invocation structural separation is explicitly not evidential independence. Live-only diagnostics compare intent separately with its sibling plan and objective final observed changes, preserving intent/plan/actual disagreement without repair, retry, normalization or authority. Legacy extraction remains the only executable plan source; malformed or missing native intent falls back to legacy_plan_derived/unavailable telemetry and cannot fail the authoritative run. Intent grants no path, write, validation, checker or merge authority and cannot add, remove, reorder or rewrite patch operations. A bounded receipt containing identities, statuses, diagnostic categories, transport/provider provenance and CHECK.1 shadow status is exported to the established durable proposal artifact directory before disposable-clone cleanup, with no raw response, prompt, source body or secret. The phase adds zero model calls, network requests, validation executions, repository traversals and patch operations, invokes no CHECK.2 or CHECK.3 path, promotes no checker and keeps all authoritative outcomes unchanged.
